open_points.subject: Browser access to the Registry API
open_points.text: “Browser — the Registry frontend from its own origin; CORS admits exactly that origin.” / “An instance reachable from beyond its host is a wrong deployment”
open_points.question: How does a staff browser reach the Registry API while the API is forbidden from being reachable beyond its host?
options: The browser runs on the Registry host or through a host-local tunnel
A public reverse proxy exposes selected Registry routes
A frontend backend calls Registry and the browser never calls it directly
open_points.default_guess: The frontend backend mediates Registry calls, so the browser does not directly reach Registry.

open_points.subject: Project identity across independent instances
open_points.text: “Registry is the single living owner of a project's identity” / “Two instances share nothing; the same physical object in two instances is two projects unless the caller gives both the same id”
open_points.question: Is ownership of a project identity scoped to one instance, and does using the same id in two instances create one logical project or merely correlate two independent records that may diverge?
options: Ownership is instance-local and equal ids only correlate independent projects
Equal ids denote one logical project despite independent stores
The same project id must not exist in multiple independent instances
open_points.default_guess: Ownership is instance-local; equal ids correlate independent projects without synchronization.

open_points.subject: Artifact status after republishing a withdrawn type
open_points.text: “Publishing a new version of a type supersedes the previous one” / “the previous published version of that type becomes `superseded`”
open_points.question: When the latest version is `withdrawn` and a new version is published, does the withdrawn pointer remain `withdrawn` or change to `superseded`?
options: It remains `withdrawn`; only a currently published pointer is superseded
open_points.default_guess: The withdrawn pointer remains `withdrawn`, and the new pointer becomes the sole published version.

open_points.subject: Loading instance configuration
open_points.text: “Service tokens, the staff credential, the artifact vocabulary (R0-08) and the frontend origin are the instance's configuration”
open_points.question: Which configuration entries are required, and what observable result occurs at startup when configuration is missing, malformed, duplicated or internally inconsistent?
options: Startup fails before the API listens
Invalid entries are ignored while the instance starts
Defaults or disabled capabilities are used for missing entries
open_points.default_guess: Startup fails before listening, with a diagnostic that does not reveal secret values.
